name: HivePunk 632
subject: Uniswap v4 hooks
thesis: Hooks are the main programmability layer on top of v4's singleton PoolManager, and Uniswap Labs continues to ship and deploy official hooks. Their value is offset by the pages' clear warning that hook bugs or malicious hooks can drain or manipulate pools, so scrutiny of the specific hook and its flags matters more than the core.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Uniswap/v4-hooks-public has 15 raw commits in the last 30 days, 4 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is 7291b9a, on 2026-10-29.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A hook is a smart contract that implements one or more callback functions from the IHooks interface.
claims.quote: A hook is a smart contract that implements one or more callback functions from the IHooks interface

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The hook specified at pool initialization is immutable and cannot be changed, removed, or swapped for that pool.
claims.quote: That hook is immutable: once a pool is initialized with a specific hook, it cannot be changed, removed, or swapped.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: v4 defines ten callbacks organized into five pairs, each wrapping a core pool action.
claims.quote: v4 defines ten callbacks organized into five pairs, each wrapping a core pool action

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Which callbacks a hook implements is encoded in the bits of the hook's deployed address, and PoolManager reads those bits to decide what to call.
claims.quote: which callbacks a hook implements isn't configured in a settings file. It's encoded in the bits of the hook's deployed address. The PoolManager reads those bits to decide what to call.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The Uniswap/v4-hooks-public repository contains the official Uniswap v4 hook contracts developed and maintained by Uniswap Labs.
claims.quote: This repository contains the official Uniswap v4 hook contracts developed and maintained by Uniswap Labs.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The official repository lists StablePairHook, VolatilePairHook, WETHHook, WstETHHook and WstETHRoutingHook.

claims.missing: A primary or on-chain data source reporting per-hook TVL, volume or fees; no page read states these figures.

risks: A single misconfigured or malicious Hook can lead to significant financial losses, denial-of-service conditions, or manipulation of the pool.
Hooks expand the attack surface because hook logic runs at key points in pool lifecycle and can modify fees, balances and swap or liquidity behavior.
Address-encoded callback permissions are a recurring source of bugs, according to the DEV article.
Hook choice is immutable per pool, so choosing a bad hook at initialization cannot be changed, removed or swapped for that pool.
Official-hook count and deployments in the pages do not by themselves prove usage volume, TVL or revenue for hooks.
unknowns: The exact permission-flag bit position for each of the ten callbacks in v4-core.: The v4-core Hooks.sol / IHooks source showing the flag constants, or an official docs page listing each bit position.
TVL, trading volume and fee revenue attributable to official v4 hooks.: A primary or on-chain data source reporting per-hook TVL, volume or fees; no page read states these figures.
wouldChangeMind: Finding the v4-core flag constants would replace the UNKNOWN on permission flags with a sourced bit-by-bit table.
Finding per-hook TVL or volume from a primary source would change the traction assessment from commit activity to actual usage.
Finding published audits for each official hook would lower the security-risk weight currently based on general hook-risk warnings.
